raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 on MI355X is slower than B200 at low concurrency in the AgentX benchmark ([InferenceX PR #3602](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3602)). One factor is the MoE sort from #36559: past its compact range, its distributed kernel scans every 64-expert chunk per pair, so with Qwen3.5's 513 experts it is slower than AITER's sort for mid-size decode batches (6 to 23 tokens). At TP8 with 16 verify tokens, going back to AITER's sort saves 1.7 ms per decode cycle.

This PR does two things:

1. Fix the slowdown: past the compact range, #36559's distributed kernel is only used up to 256 experts, and larger models go back to AITER. MiniMax-M3 (129 experts), which the kernel was written for, keeps it because it is faster there.
2. Add FP8 block-scale support to the #40204 small-M MoE kernel, which needs no sort and is much faster at small batches but only supported MXFP4.

With this PR, the interactivity improves by about 20% at concurrency 1 and 4.

## Modifications

- `moe_sorting_small.py`: past the compact kernel's range (`min(64, 2 * block_size)` (token, expert) pairs), the distributed kernel only runs for up to 256 experts; above that, the sort and the fused MXFP8 quantization go back to AITER (+13 / -3).
- `smallm_moe.hip`: `p1_body` / `p2_body` take an `F8` template flag. Shuffled FP8 weights have the same byte layout as fp4x2, so the load path is shared. e4m3 is converted to bf16 at scale 1.0 and each 128x128 block's fp32 scale is applied to the partial sum (`cvt_scalef32_pk_bf16_fp8` only applies the scale's exponent). New kernels cover TP4 (intermediate 256) and TP8 (intermediate 128); the MXFP4 kernels are unchanged.
- `smallm_moe_gfx950/__init__.py`: takes the FP8 path for shuffled `float8_e4m3fn` `w13` / `w2` with contiguous fp32 block scales, up to 20 tokens at TP4 and 48 at TP8. `SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_MOE=0` still turns the kernel off.
- `moe_runner/aiter.py`: passes `w13_scale` / `w2_scale` to `smallm_moe_supported` (+2 lines).
- Tests (MI35x suite): `TestSmallMMoeFp8Gfx950` checks both shapes against a dequantized reference at 1 / 3 / 8 tokens and the cap, and that cap+1, per-channel or non-contiguous scales, and unshuffled weights fall back. New `test_moe_sorting_small.py` compares the sort and the fused MXFP8 quant with AITER on the compact path (Qwen3.5 shape) and the distributed path (MiniMax-M3 shape, 13 to 51 tokens), and checks the fallback at 513 experts.

## Accuracy Tests

All runs use image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm720-mi35x-20260927` (same image as `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm` with that tag), InferenceX recipe flags, GSM8K 1319 questions.

| Model | Setup | Baseline | This PR |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8` | TP4, real draft acceptance, `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k` | 0.933 | 0.941 |
| `amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4-AttnFP8-V2` (sort change) | TP2, lm-eval 5-shot, thinking off | 0.977 | 0.979 |

The FP8 kernel's rel L2 against the dequantized reference is at most 7.4e-4 over 5 seeds in the unit test. The sort output matches AITER's layout in every path, so the sort change only affects speed.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

### Kernel microbenchmarks

MI355X, one GPU, CUDA graph replay, Qwen3.5-397B shapes (`E=513`, 11 slots per token, hidden 4096).

FP8 MoE layer, AITER (`per_128x128`) vs the FP8 small-M kernel, in µs:

| Tokens | TP4 AITER | TP4 kernel | Change | TP8 AITER | TP8 kernel | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 61.3 | 26.6 | −57% | 42.3 | 22.7 | −46% |
| 4 | 66.5 | 43.4 | −35% | 46.1 | 30.1 | −35% |
| 8 | 74.0 | 63.7 | −14% | 57.6 | 41.4 | −28% |
| 16 | 106.3 | 97.5 | −8% | 75.3 | 60.4 | −20% |
| 20 | 117.3 | 115.3 | −2% (cap) | 77.3 | 68.7 | −11% |
| 24 | 130.1 | 133.1 | AITER used | 84.3 | 78.0 | −7% |

TP8 caps, 60 layers rotated so the weights are not cache resident:

| Tokens | AITER | Kernel | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 24 | 68.7 | 65.2 | −5% |
| 28 | 78.2 | 75.8 | −3% |
| 32 | 83.5 | 82.9 | ~0 |
| 36 | 119.0 | 92.0 | −23% |
| 48 | 124.6 | 111.6 | −10% (cap) |

AITER moves to a slower configuration from 36 tokens, so the TP8 cap is 48 rather than 32.

MoE sort past the compact range, in µs, block size as AITER picks it. MXFP rows include the MXFP8 quant in both arms (AITER runs it as a second launch). Up to the compact range the sort is unchanged, and the FP8 small-M path does not use the sort:

| Model | Tokens | Pairs | AITER | #36559 | This PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.5 MXFP4 (sort + quant) | 7 | 77 | 10.5 | 10.3 | 10.5 |
| | 16 | 176 | 11.7 | 15.9 | 11.7 |
| | 23 | 253 | 13.5 | 15.5 | 13.5 |
| Qwen3.5 FP8 (sort only) | 16 | 176 | 6.9 | 15.7 | 6.9 |
| | 23 | 253 | 6.8 | 15.4 | 6.8 |
| MiniMax-M3 MXFP8 (`E=129`, top-4 + shared, sort + quant) | 16 | 80 | 12.0 | 8.1 | 8.1 |
| | 35 | 175 | 21.2 | 13.1 | 13.1 |
| | 51 | 255 | 24.6 | 13.0 | 13.0 |

AITER picks block size 32 for the MXFP shapes and mostly 16 for Qwen3.5 FP8, where the compact kernel covers only 1 to 2 tokens.

### AgentX benchmark

Setup:

- Hardware: MI355X, TP4.
- Model and recipe: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8` with the InferenceX recipe `qwen3.5-fp8-mi355x-sglang-agentic`, image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm720-mi35x-20260927`.
- Server flags: as in the recipe. FP8 KV cache, EAGLE 3 / 1 / 4 with simulated acceptance 3.39, admission and decode CUDA graph batch at 2x concurrency.
- Client: the CI AgentX command, `aiperf profile --scenario inferencex-agentx-mvp` on `semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126_256k`, 3600 s per run.
- Order: one run at a time on the same GPUs (this PR c1, baseline c1, baseline c4, this PR c4).

Baseline is the image as shipped: AITER's FP8 MoE with #36559's sort (`SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_MOE=0`). With this PR, every decode batch at these concurrencies runs the FP8 small-M kernel and skips the sort, so the gain here comes from the kernel.

Concurrency 1:

| Metric | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ITL p50 / p90 (ms) | 3.69 / 4.07 | 3.01 / 3.50 | −18% / −14% |
| TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) | 389 / 861 | 373 / 859 | −4% / ~0 |
| Requests completed in 3600 s | 557 | 628 | +13% |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 150 | 177 | +18% |
| Interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 271 / 283 | 332 / 349 | +23% / +23% |

Concurrency 4:

| Metric | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ITL p50 / p90 (ms) | 4.10 / 5.32 | 3.44 / 4.34 | −16% / −18% |
| TTFT p50 / p90 (ms) | 551 / 1096 | 519 / 947 | −6% / −14% |
| Requests completed in 3600 s | 926 | 992 | +7% |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 243 | 263 | +8% |
| Interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s/user) | 244 / 278 | 291 / 333 | +19% / +20% |

Each EAGLE verify pass sends 4 tokens per running request through the MoE. At TP4 the kernel therefore covers running batches of 5 or fewer, which is concurrency 4 and below here; concurrency 8 and up mostly uses AITER.

### Decode step time

Time for one EAGLE draft + verify cycle at a fixed batch size, same server flags and simulated acceptance.

TP4, image as shipped vs this PR, mean of two runs with the GPU sets swapped, in ms:

| Batch size | Baseline | This PR | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 11.89 | 9.51 | −20% |
| 4 | 16.51 | 13.08 | −21% |
| 8 | 16.35 | 16.41 | ~0 (past the cap) |

TP8, this PR with `SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_MOE=1` vs `0` (kernel vs AITER's MoE and sort), two runs per arm in ABBA order. Run-to-run noise is up to 0.23 ms:

| Batch size | Verify tokens | Change per cycle |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 16 | −0.78 ms |
| 6 | 24 | −0.51 ms |
| 7 | 28 | −0.30 ms |
| 8 | 32 | −0.07 ms (noise) |

With the kernel off at batch size 4 (176 pairs), #36559's sort takes 33.00 ms per cycle and this PR's 31.28 ms, the 1.7 ms in Motivation.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit guide.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [ ] Update documentation.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

files.patch:
@@ -294,12 +294,18 @@ def _moe_sorting_small_kernel_distributed(
             tl.store(qscale_ptr + sw, exp.to(tl.uint8))
 
 
-def _small_sort_supported(topk_ids, block_size, expert_mask, num_local_tokens):
+def _small_sort_supported(
+    topk_ids, block_size, expert_mask, num_local_tokens, num_experts
+):
     m, topk = topk_ids.shape
+    p = m * topk
     return (
         expert_mask is None
         and num_local_tokens is None
-        and m * topk <= 256
+        and p <= 256
+        # ponytail: the distributed variant scans every 64-expert chunk per pair, so it beats
+        # aiter at E=129 but loses at E=513; cutoff untuned in between
+        and ((p <= 64 and p <= 2 * block_size) or num_experts <= 256)
         and topk < 128
         and topk_ids.dtype == torch.int32
         and topk_ids.is_contiguous()
@@ -480,7 +486,11 @@ def sorting_impl_wrapper(
             and not return_local_topk_ids
             and orig_kwargs.get("output") is None
             and _small_sort_supported(
-                topk_ids, int(block_size), expert_mask, num_local_tokens
+                topk_ids,
+                int(block_size),
+                expert_mask,
+                num_local_tokens,
+                int(num_experts),
             )
         ):
             device = topk_ids.device

@@ -1,4 +1,4 @@
-"""gfx950 small-M MXFP4 fused-MoE kernel for the ROCm aiter MoE path (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B TP4 shape: hidden 4096, per-rank intermediate 256).

 MAX_TOK_DISPATCH = {256: 40}
+MAX_TOK_DISPATCH_FP8 = {256: 20, 128: 48}  # crossover vs aiter's per_128x128 asm/CK

@@ -161,8 +162,8 @@ def smallm_moe_enabled() -> bool:
     failure has disabled the kernel in this process. Numerics differ slightly from the aiter path (bf16 activations

-    per-rank intermediate 256, top-10 plus the optional fused shared expert). There is no model-name check;

+    (hidden 4096, top-10 plus the optional fused shared expert). There is no model-name check;
     smallm_moe_supported() enforces the shape, and every other model or parallel layout keeps aiter fused_moe."""
     global _available
     if os.environ.get(_ENV, "1") == "0":
@@ -194,8 +195,8 @@ def _disable(reason):
     raise SmallMMoeUnavailable(reason)
 
 
-def _get_kernels(inter: int):
-    kk = _kernels.get(inter)
+def _get_kernels(inter: int, pre: str):
+    kk = _kernels.get((pre, inter))
     if kk is None:
         global _build_dir
         if _build_dir is None:
@@ -235,14 +236,15 @@ def _get_kernels(inter: int):
         mod = _kernels["_mod"]
         try:
             kk = {
-                "p1": _Kernel(mod, f"smallm_p1_i{inter}_c16"),
+                "p1": _Kernel(mod, f"smallm{pre}_p1_i{inter}_c16"),
                 "p2": {
-                    sl: _Kernel(mod, f"smallm_p2_i{inter}_s{sl}") for sl in (10, 11)
+                    sl: _Kernel(mod, f"smallm{pre}_p2_i{inter}_s{sl}")
+                    for sl in (10, 11)
                 },
             }
         except RuntimeError as e:
             _disable(str(e))
-        _kernels[inter] = kk
+        _kernels[(pre, inter)] = kk
     return kk
 
 
@@ -271,6 +273,8 @@ def smallm_moe_supported(

+"""Small-batch MoE sorting patch (sglang.kernels.ops.moe.moe_sorting_small) vs stock aiter sorting."""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_amd_ci(est_time=20, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x")
+
+
+def _gfx950():
+    return (
+        bool(torch.version.hip)
+        and torch.cuda.is_available()
+        and torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).gcnArchName.startswith("gfx950")
+    )
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(_gfx950(), "gfx950 (MI35x) only")
+class TestMoeSortingSmall(CustomTestCase):
+    # Qwen3.5: 512 routed experts + fused shared expert, top-10 + shared slot
+    E, TOPK, DIM = 513, 11, 4096
+
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        import aiter.fused_moe as fm
+
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.moe import moe_sorting_small as S
+
+        cls.S = S
+        cls.fm = fm
+        orig_sort = fm._moe_sorting_impl
+        orig_quant = fm.fused_dynamic_mxfp8_quant_moe_sort
+        S.apply_aiter_small_moe_sort_patch()
+        if fm._moe_sorting_impl is orig_sort:
+            # an earlier import already patched aiter; recover the originals
+            orig_sort = fm._moe_sorting_impl.__wrapped__
+            orig_quant = fm.fused_dynamic_mxfp8_quant_moe_sort.__wrapped__
+        cls.orig_sort = staticmethod(orig_sort)
+        cls.orig_quant = staticmethod(orig_quant)
+        cls.dev = torch.device("cuda", 0)
+
+    def _routing(self, m, seed, E=E, topk=TOPK):
+        g = torch.Generator(device="cpu").manual_seed(seed)
+        ids = torch.stack(
+            [torch.randperm(E - 1, generator=g)[: topk - 1] for _ in range(m)]
+        )
+        ids = torch.cat([ids, torch.full((m, 1), E - 1)], 1)
+        ids = ids.to(torch.int32).to(self.dev).contiguous()
+        return ids, torch.rand(m, topk, generator=g).to(self.dev)
+
+    def _sort(self, fn, ids, w, bs, E=E):
+        return fn(ids, w, E, self.DIM, torch.bfloat16, bs, None, None, 0, True)
+
+    def _emitted_quant(self, ids, w, x, bs, E):
+        S = self.S
+        tok = S._pending_quant_input.set(x)
+        etok = S._emitted_quant.set(None)
+        try:
+            self._sort(self.fm._moe_sorting_impl, ids, w, bs, E)
+            return S._emitted_quant.get()
+        finally:
+            S._emitted_quant.reset(etok)
+            S._pending_quant_input.reset(tok)
+
+    def _assert_same_sort(self, a, b, bs, msg):
+        na, nb = int(a[3][0]), int(b[3][0])
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(a[3].cpu(), b[3].cpu()), msg)
+        self.assertTrue(
+            torch.equal(a[2][: na // bs].cpu(), b[2][: nb // bs].cpu()), msg
+        )
+        ia, wa = a[0][:na].tolist(), a[1][:na].tolist()
+        ib, wb = b[0][:nb].tolist(), b[1][:nb].tolist()
+        # the order of pairs inside one expert block is not part of the contract
+        for i in range(0, na, bs):
+            self.assertEqual(
+                sorted(zip(ia[i : i + bs], wa[i : i + bs])),
+                sorted(zip(ib[i : i + bs], wb[i : i + bs])),
+                f"{msg} block {i // bs}",
+            )
+
+    def test_sort_matches_aiter(self):
+        # compact at E=513; distributed at MiniMax-M3's E=129 / top-4 + shared
+        cases = [(513, 11, m) for m in (1, 2, 4, 5)] + [
+            (129, 5, m) for m in (13, 25, 51)
+        ]
+        for bs in (32, 64):
+            for E, topk, m in cases:
+                ids, w = self._routing(m, m, E, topk)
+                self._assert_same_sort(
+                    self._sort(self.orig_sort, ids, w, bs, E),
+                    self._sort(self.fm._moe_sorting_impl, ids, w, bs, E),
+                    bs,
+                    f"E={E} m={m} bs={bs}",
+                )
+
+    def test_fused_mxfp8_quant_matches_aiter(self):
+        bs = 32
+        # compact at E=513; distributed at MiniMax-M3's E=129 / top-4 + shared
+        for E, topk, m in ((513, 11, 1), (513, 11, 5), (129, 5, 16), (129, 5, 51)):
+            ids, w = self._routing(m, m, E, topk)
+            x = torch.randn(m, self.DIM, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=self.dev)
+            sid, sw, _, nv, _ = self._sort(self.orig_sort, ids, w, bs, E)
+            ref_q, _ = self.orig_quant(
+                x,
+                sorted_ids=sid,
+                num_valid_ids=nv,
+                token_num=m,
+                topk=topk,
+                block_size=bs,
+                sorted_weights=sw,
+                num_experts_upper_bound=E,
+            )
+            emitted = self._emitted_quant(ids, w, x, bs, E)
+            self.assertIsNotNone(emitted, f"E={E} m={m}")
+            self.assertTrue(
+                torch.equal(ref_q.view(torch.uint8), emitted[0].view(torch.uint8)),
+                f"E={E} m={m}",
+            )
+
+    def test_falls_back_to_aiter_past_compact_at_513_experts(self):
+        m = 6
+        ids, _ = self._routing(m, m)
+        self.assertFalse(self.S._small_sort_supported(ids, 32, None, None, self.E))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+@unittest.skipUnless(_gfx950(), "gfx950 (MI35x) only")
+class TestSmallMMoeFp8Gfx950(CustomTestCase):
+    """FP8 block-scale (e4m3fn, fp32 scale per 128x128 tile) at the TP4 / TP8 per-rank intermediates 256 / 128."""
+
+    E, DIM, TOPK, CAPS = 16, 4096, 10, {256: 20, 128: 48}
+
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        from aiter.ops.shuffle import shuffle_weight
+
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.moe import smallm_moe_gfx950 as M
+
+        cls.M, cls.dev, cls.w = M, torch.device("cuda", 0), {}
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        for inter in cls.CAPS:
+            q = []
+            for n, k in ((2 * inter, cls.DIM), (cls.DIM, inter)):
+                t = (
+                    torch.randn(cls.E, n // 128, 128, k // 128, 128, device=cls.dev)
+                    * 0.05
+                )
+                s = t.abs().amax(dim=(2, 4), keepdim=True) / 448.0
+                wq = (t / s).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+                deq = (wq.float() * s).view(cls.E, n, k)
+                ws = shuffle_weight(wq.view(cls.E, n, k), layout=(16, 16)).contiguous()
+                ws.is_shuffled = True
+                q.append((ws, s.view(cls.E, n // 128, k // 128).contiguous(), deq))
+            cls.w[inter] = q
+
+    def _case(self, tok):
+        # distinct routed experts per token plus the fused shared expert (E-1) in slot 10 for every token
+        ids = torch.stack([torch.randperm(self.E - 1)[: self.TOPK] for _ in range(tok)])
+        ids = torch.cat([ids, torch.full((tok, 1), self.E - 1)], 1)
+        ids = ids.to(self.dev, torch.int32).contiguous()
+        wts = torch.softmax(torch.randn(tok, self.TOPK + 1, device=self.dev), -1)
+        x = torch.randn(tok, self.DIM, device=self.dev, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        return x, ids, wts
+
+    def _supported(self, x, ids, w13, s13, w2, s2):
+        return self.M.smallm_moe_supported(
+            x, w13, w2, ids, None, False, True, False, None, s13, s2
+        )
+
+    def test_matches_reference_and_guards(self):
+        for inter, cap in self.CAPS.items():
+            (w13, s13, d13), (w2, s2, d2) = self.w[inter]
+            for tok in (1, 3, 8, cap):
+                x, ids, wts = self._case(tok)
+                self.assertTrue(self._supported(x, ids, w13, s13, w2, s2))
+                out = self.M.smallm_moe_fwd(x, w13, w2, wts, ids, s13, s2).float()
+                gu = torch.einsum("tjnk,tk->tjn", d13[ids.long()], x.float())
+                h = (
+                    torch.nn.functional.silu(gu[..., :inter]) * gu[..., inter:]
+                ).bfloat16()
+                ref = torch.einsum("tjdn,tjn,tj->td", d2[ids.long()], h.float(), wts)
+                ref = ref.bfloat16().float()
+                rel = ((out - ref).norm() / ref.norm()).item()
+                self.assertLess(rel, 2e-3, f"inter={inter} tok={tok}: rel_l2={rel:.3e}")
+            # above the cap, with per-channel or non-contiguous FP8 scales, or unshuffled weights: stay on aiter
+            x, ids, _ = self._case(cap + 1)
+            self.assertFalse(self._supported(x, ids, w13, s13, w2, s2))
+            x, ids = x[:4], ids[:4]
+            per_channel = torch.ones(self.E, 2 * inter, 1, device=self.dev)
+            self.assertFalse(self._supported(x, ids, w13, per_channel, w2, s2))
+            self.assertFalse(self._supported(x, ids, w13.clone(), s13, w2, s2))
+            self.assertFalse(self._supported(x, ids, w13, s13, w2.clone(), s2))
+            s13_strided = s13.mT.contiguous().mT
+            self.assertFalse(self._supported(x, ids, w13, s13_strided, w2, s2))
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()

reviews.body:
- Affected Scope: NVIDIA behavior is unchanged. It does not run AiterRunner or the small-sort wrapper.
- AMD Guard: The expert cutoff is the AITER small-sort wrapper, with no gfx check. The FP8 kernel runs only on gfx950, and only from AiterRunner.run.
- Unit Test Quality: The tests use unittest, check real results, and stay under 500s. Coverage is mixed at sorting_impl_wrapper, which does not fail this row.
- Accuracy evidence: The PR body reports an accuracy result.
- Performance evidence: The PR body reports a performance result.
- Flags: No new environment variable.

LGTM.
